ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are four pole-zero diagrams, respectively labeled X1(s), X2(s), X3(s), X4(s). X1(s) has one pole each on the real axis at s=-1 and s=+1, and no zero is seen. X2(s) has one pole at s=-1, and one zero at the origin s=0. X3(s) has one pole each at s=-1 and s=+1, and also has one zero at the origin s=0. X4(s) has one pole each at symmetric positions in the positive and negative directions of the imaginary axis, and also has one zero at the origin s=0. Reasoning: The Laplace transform of an even time function should satisfy X(s)=X(-s), therefore the pole-zero distribution needs to be symmetric about the origin under s -> -s, and the types and multiplicities also need to match. The two poles of X1 are located at ±1, completely symmetric, and there is no mismatched zero, so it can represent the transform of an even function. The s=-1 pole of X2 has no corresponding s=+1 pole, so it cannot. Although X3 has symmetric poles at ±1, there is a single zero at the origin, equivalent to containing an s factor, which would lead to oddness rather than evenness, so it cannot. Although X4 has symmetric imaginary-axis poles, it also has a single origin zero, likewise not satisfying the requirement for an even transform. Therefore only Figure 1 conforms.
